summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent installs a WebSocket-driven remote-shell agent granting full host control
details: On startup the package (index.js) opens a persistent WebSocket client to a configurable server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL env or config) and dispatches inbound messages through connection/message-router.js. The 'terminal_create' handler spawns a bash/pwsh PTY via node-pty and 'terminal_input' pipes remote message bytes directly into pty.write, giving the WebSocket peer an interactive shell on the installer's host. The same router exposes handlers for read_file, write_file, list_directory, create_file, delete_files, move_files, copy_files, upload_to_dir, transfer_files and git_add/reset/restore/commit/push against the configured workDir, so the remote peer also has full filesystem and git-repo control. A separate 'upgrade_agent' handler in connection/upgrade.js lets the server trigger `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and a systemd/launchd/PM2 restart on demand, giving the same peer a self-update lever over the running agent. Peer authentication is a shared secret with a weak default value ('agent-shared-secret'). service/linux.js additionally mutates the user's shell PATH (~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin). yeaft/tools/web-search.js issues outbound HTTP POSTs and ping-style probes from tool handlers reachable over the same channel.
